record.paper_title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth
record.context_brief: Second conjectured generating function for alternating unit Euler sums
record.original_question: Let G and A be the functions defined in equations (9) and (12), and let z = (1+i)t/2. Using the alternating Euler-sum notation of the source, does the identity 1 + Σ_{n=0}^{∞} [t^{2n+1} ζ(̅1, {̅1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+2} ζ(̅1, ̅1, {1, ̅1}^n)] = (1/2)(1+i) z A(z) A(-iz) {π csc(πz) - iπ csch(πz) + 4G(z)} hold whenever the right-hand side is defined?

evidence.quote: COROLLARY 2 [Conjectured in [4]). Let the functions G and A be given by (9) and (12), respectively. Then 1 + Σ [t^{2n+1} z(1,{1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+2} z(1, 1,{1, 1}^n)] = (1/2)(1 + i)zA(z)A(-iz){π csc(πz) - iπ csch(πz) + 4G(z)}, holds for all complex numbers t and z satisfying z = (1 + i)t/2 and such that the right-hand side is defined.
Other results we provide settle three of the remaining outstanding conjectures of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Alternating multiple zeta values of unit arguments are defined, for an admissible string of signed 1's, by

  ζ(ε_1, ε_2, …, ε_k) = Σ_{n_1 > n_2 > … > n_k ≥ 1} (σ_1)^{n_1} (σ_2)^{n_2} ⋯ (σ_k)^{n_k} / (n_1 n_2 ⋯ n_k),

where each ε_j is either "1" (with σ_j = +1) or "1̄" (with σ_j = −1), and where the leading entry is required to be 1̄ to ensure convergence. For a string S we write {S}^n for the n-fold concatenation of S with itself.

Define the two generating functions

  A(z) = Π_{n=1}^{∞} (1 − z^2/n^2)^{−1/2} ⋅ exp(− Σ_{k≥1} ζ(2k) z^{2k}/(2k) · 0)   — equivalently, A(z) is the analytic function determined by

  Σ_{n≥0} z^{2n} ζ({1̄, 1}^n) = A(z),

so that A(z) is the generating series whose coefficients are the alternating unit Euler sums ζ({1̄, 1}^n); and

  G(z) = Σ_{n≥0} z^{2n+1} ζ(1̄, {1, 1̄}^n),

so that G(z) is the corresponding odd-indexed generating series. Set z = (1+i)t/2 with i = √(−1).

Question. Does the identity

  1 + Σ_{n=0}^{∞} [ t^{2n+1} ζ(1̄, {1̄, 1}^n) + t^{2n+2} ζ(1̄, 1̄, {1, 1̄}^n) ]
   = (1/2)(1+i) z · A(z) · A(−iz) · { π csc(πz) − iπ csch(πz) + 4 G(z) }

hold as an identity of analytic functions in t (equivalently in z = (1+i)t/2) for all complex z at which the right-hand side is defined?
artifact.status_search_result: The identity is established as Corollary 2 of the paper by Bowman and Bradley "Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth" (Compositio Mathematica 139 (2003), 85–100; arXiv:math/0310061), where it is proved as a consequence of new arbitrary-depth multiple polylogarithm evaluations. It had previously been conjectured by Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.
